newsitem.title: ZAIRE: New Congo waits to see Kabila, new government.
newsitem.headline: New Congo waits to see Kabila, new government.

text.p: Self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila worked to form a government for his new Democratic Republic of Congo, making contact through a top aide with a veteran opponent of ousted Zaire president Mobutu Sese Seko.

But despite promises of a quick announcement of a new administration, residents of the capital Kinshasa waited in vain to catch a glimpse of Kabila and to hear details of the new team after his rebel forces captured the city five days ago.
Kabila spent his first working day on Wednesday cloistered with his closest aides in the official residence of the prime minister.

The top official of his Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) met populist opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi, but it was not clear whether there was any breakthrough in forming a new administration.
Tshisekedi presented proposals during the 55-minute meeting with Kabila's Number Two, Deogratias Bugera, which were being relayed to the AFDL leadership, opposition officials said.
Facing international pressure to form a broad-based government, Kabila stayed completely out of public view consulting a range of people on a new administration he had promised for Tuesday.
"The people of Congo are still waiting for the government of public salvation," state radio, rebaptised the Voice of Congo, said at the start of its main evening news.
A Tshisekedi aide said efforts were continuing to bring the firebrand opposition leader together with Kabila.

Wednesday's talks between Tshisekedi and Bugera, who had been consulting political and business leaders in Kinshasa since Monday, had been delayed by protocol problems, aides said. Tshisekedi insisted the meeting take place at this residence, whereas Bugera preferred his hotel.
Despite their eventual meeting, there was no indication that Tshisekedi, a populist politician sacked twice as prime minister by Mobutu, would be included in the government.
However, his fanatical followers from Kinshasa's teeming shantytowns expect him to be Kabila's prime minister.
More than 24 hours after he flew into Kinshasa unannounced after dark, residents who had earlier besieged the airport for a first glimpse of the new strongman were yet to see Kabila.
Voice of Congo said "the President of the Republic" was only provisionally installed in the prime minister's riverside residence but made no mention of his programme.

In the stunning seven-month sweep by his guerrillas across the vast country, Kabila had typically crowned the conquest of every major city with a victory rally. None has been announced for Kinshasa where security problems are far greater.
The city was the last redoubt of Mobutu's elite Special Presidential Division troops whose diehards tried to put up a last stand against Kabila's shock troops.
The Local Red Cross said it had retrieved more than 220 bodies from Kinshasa streets, many of the dead former soldiers killed in battle or by irate civilians.
Hundreds of ex-soldiers and officers have been surrendering but many are believed to have melted into the population with their weapons.
After being toppled by Kabila's forces, the ailing Mobutu escaped into exile to Togo.
Kinshasa was relatively calm on Wednesday after the scattered fighting that pervaded the immediate aftermath of the rebel takeover.
But the international airport remained closed as was the frontier across the massive Congo River into the Congolese capital Brazzaville on the opposite bank.
